newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia, UPM invigorate Helsinki, but jitters remain.
newsitem.headline: Nokia, UPM invigorate Helsinki, but jitters remain.

text.p: Shares ended higher on Wednesday, with the HEX index tacking on more than a percent after moderate trading with Nokia and UPM standing out, but doubts remained about the strength of the trend, brokers said.
"We'll live in uncertainty until the Fed's next meeting," one broker said, referring to the May FOMC meeting which may produce a move in key rates.

The HEX general index rose 1.29 percent to 2,872.82 points as advancing issues beat decliners by 66 to 23 with 26 unchanged, and the FOX derivatives and benchmark climbed 1.65 percent to end above the 1,000-mark at 1,003.45 points.
Volume was a moderate 560 million markka with 30 percent in telcoms group Nokia, which closed 3.90 markka higher at 308.90 after touching 309.00 in fair 161 million markka volume.
Nokia was helped by recent strength in U.S. tech stocks and in the dollar, brokers said.
Forestries outperformed: UPM was lively, up 5.00 to 116.00.
"The strong dollar explains UPM's gains," one broker said, but another said investors were buying in ahead of the April 11 ex-dividend date.
Tamro rose 0.40 markka to 33.00 on several block trades carried out at buy-order prices, brokers said.
Neste ended flat at 126.00 markka, recoverying from early declines as it went ex dividend.
Valmet rose 2.50 markka to 89.50, also helped by the strong dollar, brokers said.
